note: RESUME OF j583i8 AT EPOCH 8, SPEED ONLY. Same arm, same data, same objective: PAE on the full training fold, --pose-perblock-share, 2 tensors / 10,240 parameters, 15 epochs total with cosine lr 1e-2 -> 0. WHAT IS DIFFERENT IS WALL CLOCK, NOT THE MODEL: (1) the held-out PAE pass shards over cards 4,5,7 instead of running on one while two sit at a barrier -- 12.8 min -> ~4.3 expected, same 7,950 poses pooled by count under a SHARD COVERAGE assert; (2) readahead is issued from the thread that reads, so the first pose of a unit does not wait on disk the GPU could have been given; (3) the training crop is built from pose 0 rather than the union over all five, which is the SAME MASK -- crop_pose_equivalence.py finds 0 differences and identical kept-token counts, because the per-pose label permutation is within-residue (symmetric atoms swapped inside one token, so the token's atom-position set and therefore its contact distances are unchanged) -- for 88.4 -> 19.1 ms/unit of CPU. PREDICTION: cycle 46 -> ~37 min, and the held-out PAE and DockQ curves CONTINUE across the 7/8 boundary with no step. A visible step falsifies one of the three claims and is the thing to look for first. Spearman is the one steady gain, 0.243 vs shipped 0.2218. TEN-EPOCH MINIMUM still applies and epochs 1-7 carry over, so epoch 10 is the first verdict.
